memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not offer on this altar any other incense or any burnt offering or grain offering, and do not pour a drink offering on it." - Exodus 30:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God is firm about what may and may not be offered on the incense altar. No unauthorised incense, no burnt offering, no grain or drink offering. This altar had one purpose, and it was not to be repurposed for something else, however well-intentioned.

This mattered because worship is not something we design for ourselves. God determines how He is approached. Aaron's own sons would later learn this at terrible cost when they offered unauthorised fire before the Lord (Lev 10:1-2). Sincerity is not the same as obedience, and enthusiasm is no substitute for doing what God actually said.

For us the application is not about incense recipes but about the same underlying principle: we come to God on His terms, not ours. It is tempting to reshape faith around our preferences — keeping what suits us, quietly adjusting what does not. But God has revealed how we approach Him: through Christ alone, by grace, according to His Word. Jesus said true worshippers worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth (John 4:23-24). Both matter. Sincerity without truth is still strange fire.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I approaching God on His terms, or reshaping worship around my preferences?
Where might sincerity be substituting for genuine obedience in my life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You determine how You are approached, and Your way is good. Keep me from reshaping worship to suit myself, and teach me to come in spirit and in truth. Amen.
